A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TLR5 and TLR4, as well as NOD2, are involved in the host defense against Yersinia entercolitica, and that defects in the recognition pathway of these receptors may contribute to the chronic course of the infection.
chronic infections can be the result of defects in the innate immune system, which are often caused by mutations in genes encoding pattern recognition receptors (PRRs).

chronic yersinosis is caused by a combination of defects in the TRL5 and NOD-2 recognition pathways, which lead to an impaired inflammatory response.
